hook.text: What if cloud services ran in your data center but were managed by the provider? That's distributed cloud.

buildup.text: AWS Outposts, Azure Stack, and Google Distributed Cloud bring cloud services to on-premises and edge sites.

discovery.text: The provider manages hardware, updates, and APIs. You get cloud consistency with local data residency and low latency.

twist.text: Distributed cloud blurs the line between public cloud and private data centers. The distinction becomes irrelevant.

climax.text: Gartner calls distributed cloud the future of cloud computing — services everywhere, managed from one pane of glass.

punchline.text: Cloud services in your building. Managed from theirs.

quiz.question: What is the key benefit of distributed cloud?
options: Cloud-managed services that run locally for data residency and low latency
Running your own servers without any cloud provider involvement
Eliminating the need for internet connectivity entirely

details.summary: Distributed cloud extends public cloud services to multiple locations including on-premises, edge sites, and other clouds while maintaining centralized management. It lets organizations run cloud services exactly where their data or users need them without managing separate infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: Distributed cloud resolves the tension between centralized cloud management and the need for local processing. It delivers cloud benefits everywhere, not just in distant data center regions.
takeaways: Public cloud services run in customer-chosen locations
Central management maintains consistency across all locations
Data sovereignty and latency requirements drive adoption

faq.question: How does distributed cloud differ from hybrid cloud?
faq.answer: Hybrid cloud connects different infrastructure types that are managed separately. Distributed cloud runs the same public cloud services in multiple locations under unified management. The cloud provider maintains and updates the distributed infrastructure, reducing the customer's operational burden.

faq.question: What drives distributed cloud adoption?
faq.answer: Data sovereignty laws requiring local data processing, latency-sensitive applications needing nearby compute, and consistent management across dispersed operations all drive adoption. Industries like retail, manufacturing, and telecommunications benefit from compute at their physical locations.
